newsitem.title: USA: LPC -Banks back Doubletree acquisition of Red Lion.
newsitem.headline: LPC -Banks back Doubletree acquisition of Red Lion.

text.p: NEW YORK, Sept 16 (LPC) - Morgan Stanley and Bank of Nova Scotia are leading a $736 million bank loan backing Doubletree Corp's $1.1 billion cash and stock acquisition of Red Lion Hotels Inc, a Vancouver, Wash.-based chain of 56 hotels in Western states, market sources said.

Terms of the bank loan have not been finalized, but the structure tentatively includes a $100 million revolver, a $400 million amortizing term loan and a $230 million "B" term loan to be sold to institutional investors, a banker said.
Starting pricing on the credit will be tied to leverage, sources added.
About $640 million of the bank financing will be drawn for the acquisition, sources said.
Cash equity, which includes $100 million from General Electric Investments, will comprise $250-300 million of the purchase price, sources added.

The balance of the transaction is the portion Red Lion shareholders will take back when they receive $8.81 (in addition to $21.30 in cash) of Doubletree stock for each share of Red Lion stock, bankers said.
Red Lion went public last year after seven years of ownership by a unit of LBO firm Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co.

After the transaction closes, KKR and the pension funds of Washington and Oregon will own 13 percent of the combined company, existing Red Lion shareholders will own 20 percent, 45 percent will be the public float and the remaining portion is split between Doubletree, MetLife and RFS, sources said.
